I would like to also point out that currently if you have something like:

```shell
bin/infection src/Differ tests/phpunit/Git/CommandLineGitTest.php
```

You will not get any failure, despite having no mutation. This may be confusing at first glance, but those are two different scenarios: the user asked to mutate some specific files and restricted the tests. That that file has no coverage (in this case because the tests cover something else), is a legitimate outcome.

On the other hand with the symbol selection, we are validating that it _selected something_, regardless of coverage. Now part of the issue is... this is not reliable. Indeed, the selection could point to a legitimate symbol in the codebase, but it may either no be found in the current selected file subset, or, it is marked as ineligible for other reasons (e.g. not part of the git diff).

So I am really questioning if we should validate this... Maybe a better idea would be to have at debug level of verbosity a log message logging the matched symbols?

Maybe to re-explain it a bit as it's easy to loose track of the current state. We need to be able to:

- Adapt the domain code to no longer use `TestFrameworkAdapter` and use `TestFramework` instead.
- Migrate the adapters living in `infection/infection` to `TestFramework`.

But because we don't want to break compatibility with the existing external adapters which at the moment are Testo, PhpSpec and Codeception, we still need to keep all the code that depends on `TestFrameworkAdapter` somehow.

So if we are to keep a service such as `CoverageChecker` in the new adapter, we will also have a copy using the old adapter (which I will move to the Legacy directory in a sub-sequent PR for clarity).

Maybe an un-phrased question you had is why do we need to do this. From the description:

>The immediate goal is to enable the introduction of TestFrameworkFactory. This requires removing TestFrameworkAdapter from the container. Otherwise, we would need either to create another test framework instance or to bridge the new API to the old one, which is not feasible.

Reading it again I appreciate it does a poor job at going into the details, I can roughly try to answer this.

In the POC, I had services depending on both the legacy and new API, for the sake of the example let's take `CoverageChecker` (depending on the new API) and `LegacyCoverageChecker` (depending on the old one). If we keep things in the `Container` (which I believe is less overall changes), then you need to be able to do something like:

```php
            CoverageChecker::class => static function (self $container): CoverageChecker {
                $config = $container->getConfiguration();

                // The problematic statement
                $testFrameworkAdapter = $container->getTestFrameworkAdapter();

                return new CoverageChecker(...);
            },
```

`$testFrameworkAdapter = $container->getTestFrameworkAdapter()` is a problematic statement because it means, whenever `CoverageChecker` is injected, hence instantiated, we need a `TestFrameworkAdapter` instance around. Currently, it's not a problem, but once `PHPUnitAdapter` is migrated to `TestFramework` without using the legacy bridge, there is just no `TestFrameworkAdapter` instance to have anymore.

In the POC I solved it by having another `Factory` creating the legacy adapter which mean in practice, for PHPUnit, we always had 2 adapter instances around (one legacy and one new) and whilst it was fine for the POC, I didn't really like the idea either.

So this PR is a different direction: we make the adapter injectable at runtime so that we can remove `TestFrameworkAdapter` from the `Container`. This is purely for those services though, I am not suggesting that all services using a `TestFramework` instance must have it as a method parameter instead of injected in the constructor.

>where we will get it from, if container won't have it?

It is observable from this PR: in the legacy bridge we have the old adapter instance and we pass it around from there.

>if many places need TestFrameworkAdapter, does it mean we would create it multiple times? or how would/will it work?

No, with this PR we create only one instance of `TestFrameworkAdapter` at most and pass it around, so we preserve the previous behaviour we had with the `Container` which was giving a shared service.

<hr/>

I did double check the POC just in case, so no surprise once the migration is done, `Container::getTestFrameworkAdapter()` is never called (unless you use a legacy adapter like Codeception or PhpSpec).

The trouble happens in-between: for a little while, you have services instantiated that require `TestFramework` and others `TestFrameworkAdapter`. This PR does two things:

1. Use `TestFramework` for the "domain" code (i.e. anything that is not specific to to the test framework. Notable, `CoverageChecker` and the `Tracer` _are_, so they are left alone here).
2. Find a solution so what we can have an instance of `TestFramework` and `TestFrameworkAdapter` at the same time*

*: this is necessary to do the migration progressively. Otherwise, it's too much change at once.

For 2. there is several solutions that I see:

- Create two test framework instances: one for the new API and one for the old. This is what I did in the POC by having another `Factory` (see the previous explanation).
- Instead of having `TestFrameworkAdapter` in the Container, services that require it take it as a runtime parameter instead of a construction parameter. This way, they can still live in the Container as usual, but don't require a `TestFrameworkAdapter` to be instantiated.

I want to re-iterate that it is a very artificial problem stemming from trying to migrate `PHPUnitAdapter` progressively. It is technically possible to do without, but I think it's too many changes at once.

`checkRequirements()` now runs twice per invocation: here, and again in `Engine::runInitialTestSuite()` (`src/Engine.php:129`).

Before this PR the two call sites did different work - `startUp()` called `checkCoverageRequirements()`, `Engine` called `checkRequirements()`. Moving `checkCoverageRequirements()` into `checkRequirements()` (`LegacyTestFrameworkBridge.php:84`) collapsed them into the same call.

The method is not idempotent: it calls `$this->consoleOutput->logSkippingInitialTests()`, which has no dedup guard. Running `tests/e2e/Skip_Initial_Tests` on both branches:

```
master:
  [notice]  Running Infection with 1 thread.
  [warning] Skipping the initial test run can be very dangerous.   <- once

this branch:
  [warning] Skipping the initial test run can be very dangerous.   <- before the thread notice
  [notice]  Running Infection with 1 thread.
  [warning] Skipping the initial test run can be very dangerous.   <- and again
```

`checkCoverageExists()` and `checkCoverageRequirements()` also re-run, which is wasted filesystem work but otherwise harmless.

One trade-off worth naming explicitly rather than absorbing silently: on `master` the coverage requirement check ran *here*, before `mkdir($config->tmpDir)`, subscriber registration and `ApplicationExecutionWasStarted`. Moving it wholly into `Engine` means those side effects now happen before a missing-coverage-driver error surfaces. That seems acceptable, but it is a deliberate choice.

This moves the selector parse *ahead* of `looksLikeClassOrFileName()`, which silently changes what a bare PascalCase argument means.

On `master`, `infection run SomeClass` hit the `// like SomeFile or SomeFile.php - bare values behave as --filter values` branch and became a `PlainFilter` — a file filter. After this PR it parses as a source symbol selector instead. The new tests encode it: `'short class selector' => ['Plus_']` yields `([], [], [selector])`, while `'symbolic php source token' => ['Plus_.php']` still routes to `sourcePaths`.

Two consequences for anyone relying on the bare form today:

- No file filter is produced, so `SourceFilter::filtersFiles()` returns `false`, `SourceCollectorFactory::create()` gets `null`, and the whole source tree is collected and enrichment-traversed.
- If the file's class name does not match the argument, or the file declares no class at all, the run now hard-fails with `SourceSymbolNotFound` where it previously mutated the file.

Per `AGENTS.md` ("Any BC risk upgrades the prefix to `feat!:`/`fix!:` and gets a `BC break` label plus an enumerated Breaking Changes section"), this needs the title bumped to `feat!(source):` with that section — or the bare-name case kept on the old file-filter path, reserving selectors for arguments containing `::` or a namespace separator.

Pushing every `ClassLike` — anonymous classes included — means `Differ::diff` skips everything inside a `new class {...}` declared in `diff()`, and `Differ::32` can never target a line inside one.

The test `'an anonymous class does not inherit the enclosing symbol context'` shows this is deliberate, but nothing in the source says why, and a user selecting a method would reasonably expect code lexically inside it to be mutated.

Per the "explain WHY" rule, a short rationale comment here — why the enclosing context is deliberately dropped rather than inherited — would save the next reader the trip to the test.
